name: Snow
overview: Scripture presents snow both as a natural phenomenon and a powerful symbol. In the biblical lands of Palestine, Uz, and Mount Lebanon, snow is described in tangible terms, such as in Job where snow conceals the ice and is commanded by God to fall upon the earth (Job 6:16; 37:6). The imagery of snow is also used figuratively to depict purity and cleansing, as seen in Numbers where Miriam's leprosy is described as white as snow (Numbers 12:10), and in Job where washing with snow water symbolizes an attempt at purification (Job 9:30). Additionally, snow waters are portrayed as transient and vulnerable to drought, paralleling the frailty of sinners (Job 24:19).
